reason: E2 shows that 500 °C vacuum treatment minimizes wear rate and maximizes microhardness for two HEA coatings, supporting the first two premises. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for nanotwin/dislocation formation or a protective oxide scale as the mechanism, nor do they involve the FeNiCrCoCu composition, leaving the third and fourth premises unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Vacuum heat treatment at ~500 °C increases microhardness and reduces wear rate in HEA coatings
Higher temperature treatments (700–900 °C) decrease microhardness and worsen wear resistance
The improved wear resistance is due to a combination of microstructural refinement (nanotwins, dislocations) and a protective oxide scale
The specific FeNiCrCoCu composition will behave similarly to the cited CoCrFeNiNb and unspecified HEA coatings
